newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate final CPI report set for Dec 4.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate final CPI report set for Dec 4.

text.p: The Senate Finance Committee will release the final report of its bipartisan commission on the Consumer Price Index Dec. 4, Chairman William Roth said Monday in a statement.
A preliminary report by the commission released in September said the CPI overstates inflation somewhere between 0.7 and 2.0 percent.
The initial estimate of the commission, chaired by Stanford economist Michael Boskin, was that inflation may be overstated by 1.0 percent. But it left precise calculations for its final report.

Roth will be joined by Sen. Daniel Patrick Moynihan, a New York Democrat and ranking member of the committee, in releasing the report. Both Moynihan and Roth have said they believe the CPI overstates inflation.
"The commission makes it clear that the CPI is not a true cost-of-living index," Roth said. "We want to adjust benefits for changes in the cost of living, no more and no less."
The Consumer Price Index is the basis for adjusting Social Security and a host of other government payments. It is also used for indexing income taxes.
If it were adjusted downward, recipients of government checks pegged to the CPI would find their payments increasing more slowly than they otherwise would.
At the same time, taxpayers would find that income tax brackets were adjusted in their favor less than they otherwise would be to compensate for inflation.
